ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r1.claim: The reported answer that the Mighty, Knowing One created the heavens and earth is the people's own phrasing; their saying elsewhere that Allah created them does not rule out this answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r1.anchor: نفس المحكي من كلامهم، ولا يدل كونهم ذكروا في مكان خلقهن الله، أن لا يقولوا في سؤال آخر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r3.claim: Repeating خلقهن العزيز العليم in the answer intensifies emphasis; elsewhere they use Allah, the comprehensive name for the supreme attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r3.anchor: وكرر الفعل في الجواب في قوله: خلقهن العزيز العليم، مبالغة في التوكيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r4.claim: The answer matches the question in meaning rather than wording because من is a subject; a literal match would require a nominal answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r4.anchor: وجاء الجواب مطابقا للسؤال من حيث المعنى، لا من حيث اللفظ، لأن من مبتدأ.

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r1.claim: The verb is repeated for emphasis: an answer to “Who stood?” could simply be “Zayd,” but the fuller verb is stated here.
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r1.anchor: كرر الفعل للتوكيد؛ إذ لو جاء " العزيز " بغير " خلقهن " لكان كافيا، كقولك من قام؟ فيقال: زيد.

SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r2.claim: The explicit verb in the parallel confirms that Allah in 43:87 is nominative as agent, not an initial subject.
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r2.anchor: من خلقهم ليقولن الله [الزخرف: 87] مرفوعة بالفاعلية لا بالابتداء للتصريح بالفعل في نظيرتها.

SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r3.claim: The answer matches the question in meaning; matching its syntax would instead produce a nominal sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r3.anchor: وهذا الجواب مطابق للسؤال من حيث المعنى، إذ لو جاء على اللفظ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p169/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p169/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p169/r5.claim: Verses 9–15 note the opponents' confession that the Powerful and Knowledgeable God created the heavens and earth, despite their assigning partners among His servants; the universe's signs support tawḥīd and the Day of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p169/r5.anchor: The confession of the opponents of Islam that the Powerful and Knowledgeable God has created these heavens and the earth is referred to.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r1.claim: The question is coordinated with the preceding address; the verses beginning ‘How many messengers We sent’ interrupt to affirm the point and console the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r1.anchor: والآيتان أعني قوله تعالى : وكم أرسلنا اعتراض لأفادة التقرير والتسلية كما سمعت

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says disbelievers attribute creation to God, who in reality has these attributes, without necessarily uttering the titles or consciously describing Him by them; Alusi accepts this as sufficient.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r2.anchor: ذكره الزمخشري فيما نسب إليه وهذا حسب وله نظير عرفا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munir parses ‘the Mighty, the Knowing’ as the answerers’ words and the following material as God’s continuation; al-Kashf says this yields the same result as the alternative analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r3.anchor: والأظهر من حيث اللفظ ما ذكره ابن المنير

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r4.claim: Alusi finds Ibn al-Munir’s division more apparent from the wording, though either account yields quoted speech supplemented by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r4.anchor: والأظهر من حيث اللفظ ما ذكره ابن المنير

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.claim: On Ibn al-Munir’s reading, the shift to ‘We brought forth’ in verse 11 falls naturally after a change of speaker; Moses’ speech followed by ‘We brought forth’ is a parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.anchor: ونظير ذلك قوله تعالى حكاية عن موسى عليه السلام : ( لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى )

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r6.claim: Repeating the verb emphasizes creation and matches the question in meaning, as Abu Hayyan argues, though not in grammatical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r6.anchor: وفي إعادة الفعل في الجوانب اعتناء بشأنه ومطابقته للسؤال من حيث المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan notes that verbal form would not match the question grammatically: ‘who’ is the subject, so a matching answer would make ‘the Mighty, the Knowing’ the nominal subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r7.anchor: لأن من مبتدأ فلو طابق في اللفظ لكان بالاسم مبتدأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.claim: Muhammad's people admit that God, the Mighty and Knowing, created the heavens and earth, yet worship others and deny resurrection through extreme ignorance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.anchor: أقروا بأن الله خالقها، وأقروا بعزه وعلمه ثم عبدوا غيره وأنكروا قدرته على البعث لفرط جهلهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r4.claim: The attributes may be implicit in what they say, supplying its content: as elsewhere, they effectively say “God.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r4.anchor: لعله لازم مقولهم أو ما دل عليه إجمالا

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r5.claim: Alternatively, “the Mighty, Knowing” is their actual answer and the following description begins a new sentence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مقولهم وما بعده استئناف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p7/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p7/r4.claim: Asked about the earlier peoples whose histories they had heard, Quraysh would admit what they knew; God had made them generally truthful, setting up their admission about creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p7/r4.anchor: ليعترفن بما سمعوا من خبرهم لأنا لم نجعل لهم على المباهتة فيه جرأة لما طبعناهم عليه في أغلب أحوالهم من الصدق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r1.claim: Although the direct answer could have been Allah, the answer repeats the verb خلق to match the question semantically and stress their admission, intensifying their rebuke.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r1.anchor: لكنه عدل عنه إلى المطابقة المعنوية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r2.claim: The Creator’s names entail that he overcomes everything and is overcome by nothing, and that his knowledge encompasses all things and his creative power is limitless.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r2.anchor: الذي يلزم المعترف بإسناد هذا الخلق إليه أن يعترف بأنه يغلب كل شيء ولا يغلبه شيء وأن علمه محيط بكل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r3.claim: Arab idolaters admit that God created the cosmos while worshipping beings with no power or knowledge; their answer refutes their excuse and exposes deliberate obstinacy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r3.anchor: والعرب لجهلهم يعبدون مع اعترافهم بهذا غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r9.claim: After the promise of victory in 43:6, the passage exposes the contradiction of denying the Messenger for calling to one God while admitting God created all worlds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r9.anchor: لما كان قوله : { وكم أرسلنا من نبيء في الأولين } ( الزخرف : 6 ) موجها إلى الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r10.claim: Their admission that God created all things undermines worship of idols, themselves created stones; only the Creator of worshippers deserves worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p166/r10.anchor: وهل يستحق العبادة غير خالق العابدين ، ولأن الأصنام من جملة ما خلق الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r1.claim: The question shifts to an argument against associating partners with God, based on the Meccans' implicit admission that idols lack the right to worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r1.anchor: فجملة { ولئن سألتهم } معطوفة على جملة { وكم أرسلنا من نبيء في الأولين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r2.claim: The prefatory oath lām, answer lām, and emphatic nūn ensure their answer, while treating an undisputed fact as debatable dramatizes their incoherence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الكلام باللام الموطئة للقسم ولام الجواب ونون التوكيد لتحقيق أنهم يجيبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r3.claim: The staged question signals that they ignore God's creatorship in life and prayer: asked directly, they answer Allah at once, then return to shirk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r3.anchor: وإنما فرض الكشف عن عقيدتهم في صورة سؤالهم عن خالقهم للإشارة إلى أنهم غافلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r4.claim: The address may be to the Prophet, as the consolatory context suggests, or to any potential questioner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r4.anchor: للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو ظاهر سياق التسلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r5.claim: العزيز العليم names God in the narrated answer; the Meccans themselves simply said Allah, as in their answer in Luqman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r5.anchor: وليس ذكر الصفتين العليتين من مقول جوابهم وإنما حكي قولهم بالمعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r6.claim: These attributes intensify their embarrassment: they turn from the mighty, all-knowing Creator to weak, ignorant idols, while conceding God's attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r6.anchor: وإنما عدل عن اسم العلي إلى الصفتين زيادة في إفحامهم بأن الذي انصرفوا عن توحيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r7.claim: The two attributes are singled out because they oppose the idols' qualities: idols cannot even protect themselves from hands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r7.anchor: وتخصيص هاتين الصفتين بالذكر من بين بقية الصفات الإلاهية لأنها مضادة لصفات الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r8.claim: The full sense is: asked who created the heavens and earth, they say Allah; asked whether He is mighty and knowing, they affirm that too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r8.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#3/r1.claim: Their admission that God created the heavens and earth followed by worship of others exposes their ignorance, as the next verse continues the argument.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#3/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر عن جهلهم حين أقروا بأنه خالق السموات والأرض ثم عبدوا غيره بالآية التي تلي هذه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r1.claim: The polytheists would acknowledge that God alone created the heavens and earth, yet they still worship idols and rivals alongside Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r1.anchor: ليعترفن بأن الخالق لذلك هو الله [تعالى] (1) وحده لا شريك له، وهم مع هذا يعبدون معه غيره من الأصنام والأنداد.

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r1.claim: Man is an interrogative meaning who; the heavens and earth are the upper and lower cosmic bodies.

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r2.claim: Quraysh acknowledge that the Mighty, Knowing one created the cosmos, yet their worship of others exposes human ignorance.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r2.anchor: اعترافا بالصانع. {خلقهن العزيز} في حكمه وملكه. {العليم} ، بأحوال خلقه

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad says they truly attribute creation to one possessing these attributes, without necessarily using this exact title in their own wording.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : ليسندن خلقها إلى من هذا شأنه في الحقيقة. وفي نفس الأمر لا أنهم يعبرون عنه ، بهذا العنوان.

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r4.claim: Another possibility is that these were Quraysh's actual words.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r4.anchor: وقد جوز أن يكون ذلك عين عبارتهم

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r5.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r5.claim: Fath al-Rahman says the expected answer was simply that God created them; the Qur'an's wording introduces God's following attributes, distinct from the reported answer.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r5.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" ، ومقتضى جواب قريش أن يقولوا خلقهن الله ، فلما ذكر الله تعالى المعنى

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r6.claim: Primordial testimony at the covenant planted recognition of God's lordship and creation in human nature; only God's gracious attraction opens the way to His majesty.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r6.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن في جبلة الإنسان معرفةمركوزة ، وذلك لأن الله تعالى ذرأ ذريات بني آدم

BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r7.claim: The covenant's primordial affirmation bears fruit as people recognize God's creative power in this world.
BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r7.anchor: فصار ذلك الإقرار بذر ثمرة إقرارهم بخالقية الله تعالى في هذا العالم ، لكن الله تعالى لعزته لا يهتدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r1.claim: The pagans attribute creation of the heavens and earth to the one described as Mighty and Knowing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r1.anchor: لينسبن خلقها إلى الذي هذه أوصافه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.claim: The words We revived a dead land and the descriptions following the pagans’ admission are God’s speech, not theirs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.anchor: هو من قول الله لا من قولهم

MUQATIL:43:8-10/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r3.claim: If Muhammad asks the Meccan unbelievers who created the heavens and earth, they answer that the Mighty in dominion and Knowing of His creation created them.
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r3.anchor: يقول لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم: لئن سألت كفار مكة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#6/r1.claim: When asked, the polytheists acknowledge that the Mighty, All-Knowing One created the heavens and earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولئن سألتهم ﴾ اى المشركين ﴿ من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.claim: There is no pause at al-ʿAlīm because alladhī qualifies it; Abū Ḥātim allows a pause by supplying huwa before alladhī.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.anchor: ولا وقف على العليم لأن الذى صفته وقد وقف عليه أبو حاتم على تقديره هو الذى

QURTUBI-FULL:43:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:9/r1.claim: The polytheists acknowledge God created and brought the heavens and earth into existence, yet in ignorance worship others alongside Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:9/r1.anchor: فأقروا له بالخلق والإيجاد، ثم عبدوا معه غيره جهلا منهم

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r1.claim: The question could be directed to prophets or unbelievers, but the nearer antecedent is the unbelievers, who admit God created the heavens, earth, and what lies between them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r1.anchor: فقوله { ولئن سألتهم } يحتمل أن يرجع إلى الأنبياء ، ويحتمل أن يرجع إلى الكفار إلا أن الأقرب رجوعه إلى الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r2.claim: The point is that, despite admitting God is the creator, the polytheists worship others beside Him and deny His power to resurrect.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r2.anchor: والمقصود أنهم مع كونهم مقرين بهذا المعنى يعبدون معه غيره وينكرون قدرته على البعث

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r5.claim: The first divine attribute is creation of the heavens and earth; theologians make the world's origination and God's agency the first proof of God, with “created” understood as bringing into being.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r5.anchor: المتكلمون بينوا أن أول العمل بالله العلم بكونه محدثا للعالم فاعلا له

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r6.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means overpowering; the capacity for dominance comes from power, so the name signals perfect power.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r6.anchor: العزيز وهو الغالب وما لأجله يحصل المكنة من الغلبة هو القدرة وكان العزيز إشارة إلى كمال القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r7.claim: Al-ʿAlīm signals perfect knowledge; together, God's complete knowledge and power mean He can create every possible thing, after which the passage details His works.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r7.anchor: كمال العلم والقدرة إذا حصل كان الموصوف به قادرا على خلق جميع الممكنات

STUDYQURAN:43:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r1.claim: The Quraysh idolaters acknowledged one God as creator but worshipped other deities alongside Him and denied resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r1.anchor: they acknowledged that one God was responsible for creation, but they nonetheless worshipped other deities alongside Him (IK) and denied His ability to resurrect (R).

STUDYQURAN:43:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, “them” and “they” refer to the prophets, all of whom affirm that God created the heavens and earth; on this reading, 43:10–13 may continue their quotation.
STUDYQURAN:43:9/r2.anchor: Alternately, them and they can be understood as references to the prophets (R), meaning that all prophets affirm this statement.

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r1.claim: If asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists would answer that the mighty in power and vengeance, all-knowing of them and everything in them, created them.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r1.anchor: العزيز في سلطانه وانتقامه من أعدائه، العليم بهن وما فيهن من الأشياء

TABATABAI:43:6-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r8.claim: Verses 9–14 argue that God alone is Lord: the polytheists admit He created all, while His acts of creation also govern human needs; they otherwise assign governance to others.
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r8.anchor: في الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام ست آيات احتجاج على ربوبيته تعالى

TABRISI:43:6-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:6-10/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:6-10/r4.claim: Muhammad's people must admit that God created the heavens and earth; He is almighty and knows creatures' interests.
TABRISI:43:6-10/r4.anchor: أي لم يكن جوابهم في ذلك إلا أن يقولوا خلقهن يعني السموات والأرض

TABRISI:43:6-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:6-10/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:6-10/r5.claim: Their admission that God created the heavens and earth exposes their ignorance: they then worship others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
TABRISI:43:6-10/r5.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن غاية جهلهم إذ اعترفوا بأن الله خلق السموات والأرض ثم عبدوا معه غيره

THALABI:v8p328/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r9.claim: If asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists acknowledge the mighty, knowing Creator.
THALABI:v8p328/r9.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's people would acknowledge that the Mighty, Knowing God created the heavens and earth, affirming His justice and knowledge of creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ولئن سألت قومك يا محمد (¬2) {من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi calls this confession a form of faith, though they contradict it by worshiping idols alongside God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: وهذا إيمان منهم وهم يخالفون فيشركون به الأصنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r3.claim: The scholars of meaning call this the height of ignorance: they acknowledge God as creator, then associate others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: هذا إخبار عن غاية جهلهم، إذ أقروا بالله خالق السموات والأرض،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.claim: After finishing the report of their answer, God begins describing Himself in the following verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.anchor: وقد تم الإخبار عنهم (¬5) ثم ابتدأ جل وعز دالا على نفسه فقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the speech shifts from the unbelievers' reported answer to God's own description; otherwise they would say “for us,” not “for you.” The two attributes still describe the same God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.anchor: قال صاحب # النظم: أخبر الله عما يقول الكفار إذا سئلوا عمن خلق السموات

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r11.claim: Their admission that God created the heavens and earth entails affirming His might, knowledge, and the other attributes mentioned earlier.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r11.anchor: Allah’ın yarattığını itiraf ederler, bu ise onun izzetini, ilmini ve daha zikrolunan vasıflarını istilzam eyler.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.claim: The divine descriptions clarify who God is; the shift from third person to first person in the revival statement signals this clarification.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.anchor: Allah teâlâ tarafından tavzihtir. Böyle olduğuna karîne olmak üzere gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r1.claim: The pagan Arabs did not regard their idols as equal to God in every quality; they admitted that creation belongs to God alone and requires great power and knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r1.anchor: yaratma fiilinin Allah’a mahsus olduğunu, bu kâinatı ancak büyük bir güce ve bilgiye sahip bir varlığın yaratabileceğini biliyor ve itiraf ediyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r2.claim: They worshipped idols as intermediaries to God, hoping to obtain good, avoid harm, and draw near to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r2.anchor: putların işi iyiliği elde etmek, kötülüklerden korunmak için kendileri ile Allah arasında aracı olmak ve onları Allah’a yaklaştırmaktı

ITQAN:v2p533/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p533/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p533/r1.claim: The answer الله in 43:87 is not a subject-less predicate beginning a sentence; it is the subject of the verb understood in the answer, as the parallel 43:9 wording shows.
ITQAN:v2p533/r1.anchor: ومن قال في ﴿ ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله ﴾ إن الاسم الكريم مبتدأ والصواب أنه فاعل

BURHAN:v4p48/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p48/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p48/r2.claim: The wording explicitly says the heavens were created because the opponents appeared to be materialists or deniers who needed their creation stated outright.
BURHAN:v4p48/r2.anchor: لأن ظاهر أمرهم انهم كانوا معطلة ودهرية فأريد التنصيص على اعترافهم بأنها مخلوقة

BURHAN:v3p199/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p199/r5.claim: A missing predicate can be understood as the answer to an explicit question; examples ask who created the heavens and earth or sent rain, with the answer Allah.
BURHAN:v3p199/r5.anchor: الثالث أن يكون جوابا لسؤال وقع

DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.claim: Faith can refer to professing God while remaining in shirk; the People of the Book also accept some scripture while rejecting other parts and the messengers.
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.anchor: الرابع : الإيمان في شرك . كقوله تعالى في سورة يوسف
